title: Do Vision-SAE Reconstructions That Lower Loss Encode Spurious Shortcuts?

original_idea.body: Compare ViT classifications on original vs SAE-reconstructed inputs on shortcut-cue images to test whether loss-lowering reconstructions amplify spurious shortcuts; pre-trained weights.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interpretability tools amplifying shortcuts could mislead safety audits, plausible but with a gap to catastrophic risk (level 3).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pre-trained SAE + ViT classification on shortcut datasets; guided (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable with a dataset dependency (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open ViT, no lab data, externally runnable (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Pre-trained SAE + ViT inference; CPU/light-GPU feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Whether loss-lowering reconstructions encode shortcuts described as unknown; mostly novel.
